A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite changes to the title and method acronym. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention-response measurements, image and video generation experiments, acceleration comparisons, and boundary-module ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds acceleration comparisons, multiresolution evaluations, robustness studies, and failure analyses.

M1.justification: CRPA is renamed PMA, but Section 4 retains query-scale position mapping, HR key/value subsampling for LR queries, bidirectional Boundary Expand-and-Replace, and coarse/mixed/optional-fine denoising. The newly disclosed resizer training losses describe existing learned components; the PDFs do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: VBench and MSCOCO coverage is retained. Beyond v1's two-resolution experiments, including its existing 480+1920 demonstration, v2 evaluates three and four simultaneous resolution grids, reaching 3840p for video and 2560 for images (Tables 8–9 and 13–14). These substantially expand the spatial-scale combinations required of generation.

E2.justification: v2 adds standalone video comparisons with UniPC, DPM++, ToMe, TeaCache, and MagCache (Table 3). TeaCache and MagCache also become standalone image comparators, whereas v1 evaluated their integration with the proposed method. Image Table 2 adds PI+NTK; RALU, Bottleneck, and ToCa were already evaluated in v1. LR+HR disappears from Table 1, although it remains a comparator in v2 Figure 10.

E3.justification: Image evaluation replaces FID with ImageReward. The main two-stage image comparison changes from 18 steps, 7 LR steps, and 30% HR tokens to 15 steps, 5 LR steps, and 60% HR tokens; the latter setting already appeared in v1's caching appendix. The faster three-stage image setting changes from 9 to 10 steps, and Appendix C specifies DeepGazeI instead of DeepGazeIIE for images. New evaluations also introduce distilled-model and matched-latency protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained boundary and RoPE-only analyses, v2 adds saliency-model robustness (Table 6), HR key/value handling ablations (Table 15), FLUX modality-specific attention curves (Figure 16), failure cases (Figure 17), and prompt-count/timestep sensitivity checks (Figure 24). It also tests generation with and without DyPE. v1's FID-versus-token-ratio plot and four-budget image comparison are absent; v2 introduces a video quality–latency comparison.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 documents attention-measurement sample counts and checks larger prompt samples, but retains the same averaging estimator and does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive acceleration, distillation, multiresolution, and ablation results. For example, Table 5 newly reports four-step DMD at 80.15 VBench total and 10.9 seconds, versus DMD plus the proposed method at 80.11 and 5.6 seconds. Image comparison entries are revised under changed settings, and FID results are removed. Many retained video and boundary-ablation scores merely receive percentage formatting or additional precision.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 changes S from native grid spacing in v1 to native resolution scale, explicitly larger for HR, in v2. This corrects the interpretation of alpha = S_q/S_k to agree with the retained stretching examples. The sinusoidal decomposition and its proof are unchanged apart from formatting and relocation from Appendix A to B.

C1.justification: The central diagnosis, training-free attention correction, boundary refinement, and efficient image/video generation claims remain. v2 drops v1's sweeping statements that the method stabilizes all heads and layers uniformly and is compatible with any pretrained DiT, modestly narrowing the claimed applicability.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning modality-dependent learned RoPE biases, LR queries' reliance on coarse context, and high-resolution performance through token counts closer to training conditions. Appendix E replaces v1's discussion of unstable ultra-high-resolution details with concrete texture-transition failures and proposals for better masks and retrained positional encodings. These substantially revise the explanation of applicability and remaining limitations.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents resizer training pairs, Pexels and Aesthetic-Train-V2 data, batch size, and weighted latent/pixel reconstruction and LPIPS losses. Appendix C adds attention-probing sample counts and offset grids, stage schedules, caching thresholds, and baseline configurations. A project-page link is also added. These disclosures materially improve reproducibility without establishing that previously unspecified training procedures changed.

R1.justification: The distinction from RoPE extrapolation and positioning relative to RALU remain. v2 adds an explicit claim to be the first work focused on mixed-resolution generation, cites additional mixed-resolution vision precedents, and adds references supporting DyPE, distillation, ImageReward, and training data. Some earlier references, including FID and VideoRoPE, disappear. The principal research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around generation efficiency and positional scale bias. The title and method terminology change, method explanations are substantially revised, and experiments are reorganized by comparison type. The appendix gains subsections and a figure guide, with results moved before the derivation.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column main layout to a single-column format. Figure 1 becomes a sample montage, Figure 4 is redrawn to contrast both interpolation baselines with PMA, and qualitative comparisons are redesigned with detail crops. Numerous new tables and analysis figures are added, while retained material such as the boundary-ablation table moves into the main text.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and reproducibility: new standalone video acceleration comparisons, saliency and key/value ablations, multigrid tests, and concrete failure cases address important gaps in v1. Resizer training and experimental configuration disclosures make the work easier to assess and reproduce. Removing FID analyses reduces continuity, and changed image protocols prevent straightforward historical performance comparisons. Nevertheless, the targeted evidence and documentation gains provide a substantial overall improvement without requiring a new method.
